title: security: rbac-v2 enforce KMS region residency + audit logging enhancements
author: Asha Patel
description: Summary: enforce KMS region residency constraints in RBAC v2 policies and improve audit logging for residency decisions. Motivation: customers in regulated industries require deterministic enforcement and auditable decisions when a request references a KMS key outside allowed regions. This change adds enforcement hooks, policy schema fields, richer audit events, unit/integration tests, and docs. Changes: 1) extend RBAC v2 policy schema with `kms_residency` and `kms_region_pinning` fields that can be set on roles and resources; 2) policy enforcer will evaluate residency constraints at request-time and return a clear DENY with reason when a KMS key is out-of-residency; 3) audit logging now emits structured (key=value) residency_decision events including requested_key_region, allowed_regions, policy_id, request_id, eval_path, and decision_reason; 4) introduce an opt-in enforcement toggle `rbac.enforcement.kms_residency=true` with migration path from `audit-only` to `enforce`; 5) add integration test harness that spins up minimal KMS mock to validate routing and enforcement behavior. Checklist: - [x] Schema changes implemented and backward-compatible (defaults to audit-only) - [x] Enforcer integration and unit tests added - [x] Audit log format documented and included in observability pack - [x] Migration guide added to docs and release notes - [x] CI pipelines updated with new integration job - [x] Security scan reviewed and accepted Related: Linear ENG-4123, SEC-98. See docs: docs/security/rbac_v2.md#kms-residency and internal runbook link https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4123 for rollout plan. Rollout: staged feature-flag rollout over 2 weeks, starting in canary, then controlled by workspace-level flag for Dedicated customers. Backwards compatibility: policy schema defaults to audit-only so existing policies keep behavior until enforcement flag enabled.
